facts.text: Founded by the Dutch in 1631, Georgetown is Delaware’s first colony and the earliest European settlement in the region.
The town was named Georgetown after commissioner George Mitchell, who led the 1791 land purchase that established the county seat.
The historic Sussex County Courthouse at “The Circle” was restored in 1976 and is now managed by the Georgetown Historical Society.
Pennsylvania Railroad passenger trains ran through Georgetown until the late 1940s, and today the Delmarva Central Railroad operates the Indian River Subdivision freight line.
The Georgetown Historical Society offers weekly courthouse tours, and the surrounding historic district is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Georgetown serves as Sussex County’s seat and is famously described as “sixteen miles from everywhere” because of its central location.
